absent: Probe control block and probe descriptor field layouts and status value encodings.
Semantics of nested reentry, single-step setup and resume, and post-processing helpers.
Out-of-line template instruction bytes and calling convention beyond patched field positions.
Memory ordering and failure modes of text publication and cross-CPU synchronization.
Boot parameter block and setup payload binary layouts and version meaning.
KVM async fault and steal-time activation protocol and static key lifecycle.
Sysfs attribute permission encoding and object lifetime rules beyond create and remove pairing.

findings.text: Kernel breakpoint trap entry for probes. Declines user-mode traps. Claims traps whose faulting address hosts a registered probe and traps representing completion of probe single-step, reporting handled; all other traps are left for generic handling.

Probe hit lifecycle distinguishes fresh hit, nested reentry, and single-step completion. Fresh hit enters active state and may invoke a pre-handler whose veto suppresses stepping; reentry delegates to nested handling; a fault inside the relocated copy is treated as step completion with resume plus post processing.
Breakpoint and debug-trap probe processing executes in a non-preemptible interrupt-masked context, including the single-step window where the interrupt flag is cleared.

Faults occurring while executing the relocated probe copy are attributed to stepping. The trap location is rewound to the original probe address and prior interrupt flag state is merged back before clearing current probe context.
Architecture probe initialization exposes blacklist population covering the entry text range, a trivially successful init, and a trampoline query that never claims trampoline status.

Alternative probe entry driven by function tracing rather than breakpoint exception. Ignores invocations while globally disabled or under recursion contention, ignores missing or disabled probes, and counts nested hits as missed instead of handling them.
Tracing probe path serializes against tracing recursion with a try-acquire and release pair held for the whole lookup and handling window, abandoning work when acquisition fails.

When handling, the tracing path presents a breakpoint-like register view, marks the probe active, runs the optional pre-handler, optionally emulates single-step completion including the post-handler, restores the original location, and releases current probe.
Tracing preparation leaves no out-of-line copy and marks the probe non-boostable, signalling that execution proceeds via tracing rather than copied instructions.

Optimized probe template layout is expressed as byte distances from the template entry to the privileged-state, argument, call, and end positions, allowing the builder to patch a copy without hardcoding absolute addresses.

Out-of-line buffer patching is capability and width sensitive: privileged-state clearing is omitted on CPUs without the relevant mitigation feature, and the probe-argument move uses the width appropriate to the build.

Detour target invoked when execution is redirected to an optimized probe slot. Ignores disabled probes, compensates for the synthetic call frame, establishes kernel execution context and probe-hit register view, runs the optimized pre-handler, and maintains accurate current-probe tracking.
Detour execution runs with preemption inhibited across current-probe assignment and handler invocation, and treats a hit while another probe is current as a missed count rather than nested execution.

Out-of-line copying covers at least the size of the replacing jump using only relocatable boostable instructions and fails when the source range overlaps tracing, jump-label, or static-call reserved text.

Optimization eligibility uses instruction decoding to detect indirect control transfer and relative branches whose target falls inside the bytes that would be overwritten plus displacement, vetoing optimization in either case.

A probe site is optimizable only when its containing function is known and large enough, lies outside entry text, contains no exception-table entry, decodes cleanly without debugger breakpoints, has no indirect transfer where jump tables are possible, and has no branch into the patch window.
Optimized range bookkeeping rejects arming when another armed probe lies inside the copied span and provides a containment test for an address relative to the optimized probe base and length.

Optimized probe storage moves between absent, prepared, and removed. Preparation requires eligibility, buffer and slot allocation, and reachable displacement; it assembles template plus relocated instructions plus probe call plus return transfer and publishes the slot. Removal optionally records the change, releases the slot, and clears stored pointer and length.

Activation preserves the bytes following the initial breakpoint byte, then replaces the full jump-sized window at each listed probe with a relative transfer to its out-of-line slot and removes the probe from the pending set, asserting probes are enabled.

Deactivation restores the breakpoint byte first, synchronizes all CPUs, then restores the trailing bytes and synchronizes again before reporting the text change; list form applies this to every entry and moves each to a completion list.
Boot parameter sysfs exposes a read-only version identifier in hexadecimal form and a read-only binary view over the in-memory boot parameter block.
Firmware setup payloads form a physical-address linked list. Index-based lookup, counting, and sizing walk the chain through short-lived mappings, interpreting object names as decimal indices.

One level of indirection is transparent for type, size, and payload retrieval; nested indirection is exposed as opaque outer bytes rather than followed further, and reads are bounds-checked and truncated to the available length with empty and over-range handling.

Sysfs hierarchy presents numbered child nodes under a setup container, each with type and sized payload views. Construction creates the container, sizes each child before attaching its group, and unwinds created nodes on failure; teardown detaches the group and releases references.

Guest logging uses a fixed textual prefix. Asynchronous fault and steal-time accounting default to enabled with boot options to disable each, a read-only static key tracks async fault availability, and per-CPU state records whether async faults are active on that CPU.
